mainKeyword: best rv air conditioner for fifth wheel
guideTitle: Best RV Air Conditioners for Fifth Wheels (2026)
metaTitle: Best RV Air Conditioners for Fifth Wheels
metaDescription: Six rooftop air conditioners for fifth wheels compared on roof height clearance, ducted versus non-ducted fit, multi-unit loads and rear-bedroom comfort.
expertTake: The Coleman-Mach 10 Signature Series R32 is the fifth-wheel pick for anyone who needs to keep overall height down, since Coleman pitches its low profile at fifth wheels directly. The RecPro 15K ducted heat pump is the answer for a coach with a ceiling duct network. Skip the 18,000 BTU units if your fifth wheel has only a 30 amp inlet, because a big unit and a small inlet is a recipe for tripped breakers.
introParagraphs: A fifth wheel is tall, long and usually split across two levels, with a bedroom up front over the hitch and a living area in the middle. That shape makes cooling a distribution problem as much as a capacity one, and it puts the roof close to the legal height limit on many roads.

Buyers often have to choose between a unit that fits the existing ceiling and one that gives the most cooling. The better question is which ceiling system the coach already has, how much height can be spared and how many units the supply can carry. We rank picks against those three practical limits.

products.name: Coleman-Mach 10 Signature Series R32 low-profile RV AC
products.description:
Coleman describes the Mach 10 Signature as a low-profile unit and calls out fifth wheels and trailers as the target, a rare piece of direct positioning. In a rig that sits close to the legal height limit, a lower shroud is real clearance. The R32 refrigerant keeps the charge smaller by weight than older R410A designs.

It is a conventional design, which means the parts, the service knowledge and the ceiling compatibility are about as good as the industry gets. That matters on a fifth wheel that spends long seasons parked, where a failure in the middle of summer needs a quick fix. The listing does not state a BTU figure, so check the model code against your coach's capacity.

Compared with the Dometic 13.5K it brings the Coleman ecosystem and a lower profile for similar service access. Wash the filter often, inspect the roof gasket and check the shroud screws after the first trip.
products.bestFor: Fifth wheels where height clearance and parts support both matter.
pros: Low-profile design aimed at fifth wheels
R32 refrigerant with a smaller charge
Established brand with wide parts support
cons: Capacity is not stated in the listing

products.name: RecPro 15K ducted air conditioner with heat pump, black
products.description:
Many fifth wheels, especially larger models, use a ducted ceiling to push cold air to the rear bedroom, and the RecPro 15K ducted unit is built for exactly that. A built-in heat pump adds mild-weather warmth and the maker claims 55.4 dB of noise.

A ducted layout evens out the temperature across a long coach, which is useful when the front bedroom sits a long way from the living area. It will not fit a non-ducted ceiling, so check the interior before ordering. The heat pump weakens as the outdoor air approaches freezing.

Against the 13.5K cooling-only RecPro it adds capacity and heat at a higher price. A fixed-speed compressor surges at startup, so a soft start is wise on a generator. Wash the return filter monthly and check the gasket annually.
products.bestFor: Ducted fifth wheels that need even cooling to a rear bedroom.
pros: Ducted design spreads air through the coach
cons: Will not fit a non-ducted ceiling

products.name: LAOFINA 18,000 BTU non-ducted heat pump, 50 dB claim
products.description:
For a big fifth wheel with tall ceilings and a lot of glass, 18,000 BTU is a sensible starting point, and the LAOFINA pairs it with a heat pump and a stated 50 dB. It is a non-ducted unit, so it suits a coach with a center ceiling assembly.

Its big compressor is also its liability on a smaller electrical system. On a 30 amp inlet it should run alone or with a soft start, and on a 50 amp coach it works well with careful load management. Like other LAOFINA units it needs both 115V AC and 12V DC power.

Against the RecPro it offers more capacity and a lower noise claim but a non-ducted layout. Check your supply before buying, keep the filter clean and inspect the DC feed whenever the batteries are serviced.
products.bestFor: Large non-ducted fifth wheels with a 50 amp inlet.
pros: 18,000 BTU for tall, glassy fifth wheels
cons: Big compressor strains a 30 amp inlet

products.name: Arsenda 18,000 BTU RV AC heat pump, 110-120V non-ducted
products.description:
Arsenda uses R32 refrigerant in this 18,000 BTU heat pump, which the maker says cools faster and uses less energy. It is a non-ducted unit with a rugged construction aimed at travel, and it suits a large fifth wheel's living area.

The cost of 18,000 BTU is startup load, so a soft start is wise on a generator and a 50 amp inlet is the realistic minimum for comfort with other appliances. It also requires both 115V AC and 12V DC power, so a weak house battery can stop it.

Compared with the LAOFINA it offers similar capacity with R32 called out in the listing. A fifth wheel with two or three units can pair it with a smaller unit in the bedroom. Check the DC feed, wash the filter and inspect the roof bolts each season. Owners of tall fifth wheels also benefit from a roof walk once a year to look for lifting sealant around every curb.
products.bestFor: Living-area units on big fifth wheels with 50 amp service.
cons: Large startup load on small supplies

products.name: Dometic FreshJet 3 Series 13.5K BTU rooftop AC, white

specList.label: Weight claim
specList.value: About 64 lb for the lightest model

products.description:
A fifth wheel's roof is high off the ground, which makes unit weight a safety issue for whoever lifts it into place. Dometic says its lightest FreshJet 3 version weighs about 64 pounds, 14 percent lighter than its previous lightest model, and claims a 4 dB noise reduction.

At 13,500 BTU it suits a bedroom zone or a smaller fifth wheel, and a second unit can cover the living area. It reuses existing mounting on many coaches, and Dometic parts are the easiest to find on the road.

Compared with the Coleman Mach 10 it offers a stated capacity and weight but a taller shroud. A fixed-speed compressor means staggering startups on a multi-unit coach. Rinse the filter every month and check the gasket each spring.
products.bestFor: Bedroom zones and smaller fifth wheels where lifting is a concern.
pros: About 64 lb makes roof lifting safer
Best parts support in the industry
cons: Smaller capacity for large living areas

products.name: RecPro 13.5K non-ducted RV AC, cooling only, white
products.description:
A fifth wheel with two or three units does not need every one to be premium, and the RecPro 13.5K cooling-only model is the practical choice for a secondary zone. It claims a low amp draw and 59.7 dB of noise, with a UV-resistant shroud.

Cooling only keeps cost and complexity down, and 13,500 BTU is a standard size for a bedroom or loft. The noise claim is the loosest in this guide, so it is better used where sleepers are not directly beneath it.

Against the Dometic it costs less and has less brand support. A single-stage compressor surges at startup, so stagger it with other units. Keep the filter clean monthly and check the roof gasket annually.
products.bestFor: Secondary zones where cost matters more than sound.
pros: Low amp draw claim helps multi-unit loads
cons: 59.7 dB claim is the loudest here

buyingCriteria.explanation: Fifth wheels are tall, and many sit close to the typical 13 feet 6 inch road limit once the roof unit is added. A low-profile unit such as the Coleman-Mach 10 Signature gives a few inches of margin. Measure your travel height with all roof gear and compare it with your planned route before buying.

Larger fifth wheels often use ducted ceilings that feed the rear bedroom through trunks, while smaller ones use a center assembly. The RecPro 15K is ducted, and the LAOFINA, Arsenda and RecPro 13.5K are non-ducted. Look at the ceiling before ordering, since a mismatch means a remodel.

A fifth wheel commonly carries two or three rooftop units and a 50 amp service. Each draws roughly 12 to 16 amps while running, and the starting surges are higher. Two units plus modest loads is realistic on 50 amps, and soft starts or a load-management system keep the surges from tripping the breaker.

A tall living area with big windows may need 15,000 to 18,000 BTU, while a bedroom or loft is fine with 13,500 BTU. Splitting the load across zones usually works better than one huge unit. Walk the coach on a hot afternoon to see which room lags before choosing. A cheap infrared thermometer pointed at the ceiling and floor of each room tells you where the cooling is actually landing.

A long fifth wheel can leave the rear bedroom warm even when the living area is cool. A ducted unit like the RecPro helps by pushing air through the ceiling, while a separate bedroom unit solves it directly. Check your layout before assuming one unit can reach the back.

Rooftop units weigh 70 to 110 pounds, and the roof of a fifth wheel is far above the ground. The Dometic 13.5K is listed at about 64 pounds in its lightest version. Use a rope-and-pulley or a lift, never a ladder carry, and work in calm weather with two helpers. A fifth wheel roof can be fourteen feet up, so a fall or a dropped unit is serious, and a rented lift is cheap compared with either.

howWeEvaluated.title: Height and profile
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at low-profile claims, giving credit to the Coleman-Mach 10 Signature for its fifth-wheel positioning. Unit weight, such as Dometic's 64 lb claim, also counted. We noted where no height figure was given.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ceiling compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated ducted from non-ducted designs and flagged the RecPro 15K as the only ducted pick. Many fifth wheels use ducts, so we weighted this heavily. A mismatch costs more than the unit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Multi-unit load
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered running draw, startup surge and heating method across several units. Units with a low amp claim scored for multi-unit coaches. Large compressors were flagged for soft starts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Zone fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched 13,500 BTU units to bedrooms and 15,000 to 18,000 BTU units to living areas. Oversized units in small zones were marked down. Heat pumps earned credit for shoulder seasons.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support and parts
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered brand parts stock and technician familiarity, with Coleman and Dometic leading. A fifth wheel often stays in one place for months, so service matters. Cheaper brands were credited for price.

howToChoose.subheading: One Large Unit vs Two Smaller Units

cards.label: One large unit
cards.text: An 18,000 BTU unit like the Arsenda cools a big living area, but it carries the biggest startup surge and may leave the bedroom warm.

cards.label: Two smaller units
cards.text: A 15,000 BTU living unit plus a 13,500 BTU bedroom unit spreads the load and the comfort, at the cost of two roof openings.

howToChoose.note: Two units for large coaches with a 50 amp inlet; one large unit if the ceiling allows only one opening.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A ducted unit that reaches the back, or a dedicated bedroom unit. Check that the vents are open and the duct is unkinked.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The RecPro 15K ducted pushes air along the coach. The Dometic 13.5K is a light bedroom-zone choice.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your fifth wheel is your full-time home or sits near height limits. The Coleman-Mach 10 and RecPro 15K repay in fit and comfort.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You use the coach for short seasonal trips. The RecPro 13.5K works.

maintenance.why: A fifth wheel has several filters across zones, and a clogged one freezes its own coil. Keep a calendar.
A tall roof flexes in wind, which cracks sealant. A leak in the bedroom area is costly, and the water often travels along the roof deck before it shows up on the ceiling far from the actual crack.
On ducted systems a loose trunk leaks cold air into the ceiling. Check the joints from the attic side if accessible.
Road vibration loosens hardware and shifts the gasket. Even torque keeps the seal.
The LAOFINA and Arsenda need 12V DC alongside shore power. A corroded terminal stops them.

faq.q: What size air conditioner does a fifth wheel need?
faq.a: Most fifth wheels need two units, with 13,500 BTU for a bedroom and 15,000 BTU or more for the living area. The best size depends on sun, slides and insulation. A fifth wheel with a tall front bedroom and a glass-heavy living area behaves like two separate rooms, so match each zone to its own unit instead of averaging the total.

faq.q: Is my fifth wheel ducted or non-ducted?
faq.a: Look at the ceiling. Branching vents along the ceiling mean ducted, and one center assembly means non-ducted. Replacement parts differ, so confirm before ordering. If you cannot tell, remove one ceiling panel and look: a plenum box with duct trunks leaving it is ducted, while a plain opening with a single louvered cover is not.

faq.q: Can I run two air conditioners on 50 amps?
faq.a: Usually yes, with care. Two units plus modest loads fit, but starting surges and a water heater element can trip the breaker, so stagger starts. Many full-timers add an energy management system, which sheds the water heater and other big loads automatically whenever a compressor is starting.

faq.q: How much height does a low-profile unit save?
faq.a: A few inches compared with a standard shroud. It matters for a fifth wheel near the road height limit but not for one with plenty of clearance. Drive the route in your head: gas station canopies, drive-through overhangs and low tree limbs are where a few extra inches buy peace of mind.

faq.q: Do I need a soft start?
faq.a: On a generator, usually. Fixed-speed compressors surge at startup, and a soft start reduces it sharply for a small cost. On a fifth wheel with two units the saving compounds, because each soft start lets the generator or the pedestal absorb the surges one after another instead of together.

faq.q: Why is my rear bedroom so warm?
faq.a: A long coach loses cold air along the way, and a single unit may not reach the back. A ducted unit or a bedroom unit fixes it. Closing interior doors, opening the bedroom vents fully and running the unit's fan on a higher setting are free steps that sometimes close the gap before any hardware is bought.
